Dec. 16 - Caramel secrets:
- Put 1/2 cup sugar plus 1 tbsp water in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Add 1/8 tsp cream of tartar along with the sugar.
- Twirl as soon as the sugar starts melting and continue until all the dry sugar is dissolved or melted. Take care not to burn it during this step; browning happens after the sugar has melted/dissolved.
- When the solution starts to become reddish, turn down the flame and move the pan off the heat.
- Add 1/4 cup warm water to the pan. It will solidify on the bottom; put the pan back on the heat and swirl the liquid to dissolve/release the hardened caramel.
- Take care not to brown it too much. Take the pan off the heat and pour the liquid caramel into a heatproof container (mason jar or glass measuring cup).

Total quantity: two 8-inch loaf pans [8 x 2 1/2 x 3 1/2] and one 5-inch loaf pan [5.75 x 3 inches].

- Used 1 lb ground beef, 80/20.

1/12/21 - 3.5 stars

- Using 1.75 lb made 22 meatballs.
- Used 1 lb ground beef and 1 lb ground pork.

Thai-Style Spare Ribs notes:

5/30/21 - 3.5 stars
- Long cooking time. Followed the NYT recommendation: 2 hours at 275 F, flipping and basting every 30 minutes. Next time double the marinade.
- Overall flavor was okay, but it did not come out sweet. It was mostly sour, and the meat was tough/chewy. It would have been better sweeter and falling off the bone.

- Bought one rack of baby back ribs, 3.11 lb, and cut it into 3 pieces of about 5 ribs each.
- Served with rice.

7/11/21 - 3.5 stars

- Used the same marinade recipe; should have made it sweeter with more honey/maple sugar. It was too sour. Use less tamarind paste next time.

Lamb Keema Matar notes:
- The recipe came out really good. The only complaint was that it was not spicy enough. Should have added more black pepper, or some whole peppercorns to the spice mix at the beginning. Other than that it was excellent.

10/12 - Second attempt came out better than before.
Changes:
- Used only 3 cardamom pods, 1 piece cinnamon, and added about 6-8 peppercorns initially.
- Used 1 tomato, 1 potato, and 1 cup peas.
- Added 1/4 tsp red chili powder.
- Not sure what the nutmeg adds to the dish.
- Added about 3 tbsp yogurt.

12/5 - [rating appears to be 3 stars]
- Used 1.85 lb stew beef (beef round), sufficient for 3 people.
- Doubled the recipe for the ground spice mixture.
- Pressure-cooked the beef for 28 minutes, then cooked uncovered for 7 minutes to dry it out. The beef came out feathered; perhaps cook it for less time. Some cubes were quite large, so cut them smaller.
- Did not add garam masala.
- Salt: 1 1/4 tsp.

Feb. 20

- Grilled for 1 minute, then left it on the cooler side for 1.5 minutes. Skip this step next time.

Egg Roast notes:
5/16/20 - 4 stars
- Needed a little more sauce in the onion gravy; a bit more water at the end would have done it.
- Also added 2 tsp tomato paste; can skip this next time.
- Did not add the sugar, but should have done so before adding the eggs.

Chettinad Egg Curry - 10/17, first attempt: Really good; will make again.
- Used 4 tsp tomato paste with 1 cup water instead of puree.
- Used only 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste; maybe should have used 1.5 tbsp.
- Next time slice the eggs in half and fry.
- Interesting flavor of vinegar and roasted coconut; it reminded me of the red chutney for dosa.
- Reduce Kashmiri chili powder to 1/2 tbsp.
- Reduce black peppercorn to 1/2 tbsp (used 1 tbsp).
- Took a long time to make: 1.5 hours.
- Ingredient annotation: 7 eggs, boiled for 10 minutes.

Chettinad Egg Curry continuation:
Attempt #2 (11/13) - 3/5, not so good.
1. Boiled eggs starting in cold water for 12 minutes over a medium-hot flame, with a rolling boil toward the end. Did not put the eggs into an ice bath immediately after cooking. Next time start the eggs in rolling boiling water for 12 minutes, ice-bath immediately, and use running water to peel if the shells are too sticky.
2. Roasted the coconut powder too much. It should only be heated lightly over a low flame for a nice aroma. Also possibly added too much coriander powder.
3. Added 6 tsp tomato paste to 1 1/2 cups water (possibly too much). Did not cook this down enough to sweeten the dish a bit.

Attempt #3 (11/15) - 3/5, not good.
1. Boiled 8 eggs in boiling water for 12 minutes and then immersed them in cold water. Peeling the shells was not too difficult.
2. Used frozen coconut; not sure there was much flavor because it was too wet to get dry enough by roasting. Stick with dry coconut next time.
3. Worst mistake: used canned tomato sauce. It was too acidic and had a strong vinegary flavor, which ruined the dish. Do not use canned sauce; stick with tomato paste and water.

- Also made the pickled onions; they were a good side for the tacos.

[Date unclear] - 2 stars
- Chicken was good with the pan gravy; cooked at 475 F for 30 minutes.
- Skip the olive and parsley mixture; it was kind of mediocre.

- Used 3 dry red chilies instead of 8.
- Replaced the ginger and garlic with 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste.
- Dry-roasted the spices and ground them.
- Fried onions with ginger-garlic paste and green chilies.
- Added tomatoes, sauteed them, and added the ground mixture.
- Added the meat to the tomato mixture.
- Cooked over medium-high heat for 1 hour, then simmered for 30 minutes after adding potatoes.
- Recipe was okay. The rogan josh recipe was better; should try it with goat instead.

Mutton Rogan Josh annotation:
- 3 1/2 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder is way too much; reduce to 1 tbsp.

- Soaked 1 cup rice for 30 minutes and drained for 10 minutes.

Porchetta Pork Roast notes - 12/25/21:
- Used a 7.5 lb bone-in pork shoulder.
- Marinade: fresh sage, 2 tsp dried rosemary, 7 garlic cloves, 1.5 tbsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper flakes, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1/4 cup olive oil, 1 tsp fennel seeds, and zest of 1.5 lemons. Blended in a food processor; use the blender next time.
